core.title: Reconcile delivered behavior with declared intent before accepting a delivery
core.given: A delivery whose deterministic CI and convention gates are green is offered for final acceptance
core.when: the final reviewer decides whether to accept it
core.then: Produce a durable APPROVE, RETURN or ESCALATE decision on whether the delivered behavior of the assembled system is the intended behavior.
prefer: Intent first: before relying on diff or implementation, read the delivery's declared intent — the acceptance criteria, the responsibilities, behavior sequences and routing decisions declared in the plan artifacts, the user-facing journey, and delivery criteria when available (the concrete intent sections are the stack's plan-intent sections, from the profile); state the externally meaningful behavior that should be observable if the delivery is correct.

Choose the highest meaningful assembled boundary: the real user-facing journey for human-facing behavior, the exposed assembled interface for API/runtime behavior, the production routing and sequencing path when routing is material to the claim.

Exercise the real production path (see unless[1]) with the minimum inputs needed; observe user-visible outcomes, API responses, persisted effects, emitted events, route selection plus its business outcome, or other effects the plan names.

Reconcile three sources independently; all must materially agree: (1) declared intent: what plan and delivery criteria require; (2) executable proof: what the stack's acceptance, smoke and end-to-end tests (the executable-proof kinds) actually prove; (3) observed runtime: what the assembled system does through the real boundary. No single source suffices: passing tests alone are insufficient because a test may have drifted with the implementation; observed runtime alone is insufficient if it no longer satisfies declared intent; a correct plan whose implementation is unexercised or unreachable is also incomplete.

Look for: missing required behavior; intended behavior unreachable through the assembled system; materially unexpected new behavior; a routing decision selecting the wrong behavior path; a composed behavior sequence yielding a different business outcome than declared; a journey's final user-visible result differing from intent; passing tests proving a different behavior than the plan; acceptance or planning artifacts silently changed to match the implementation without authorized intent change.
Inspect diff and implementation only after expected behavior is set, to explain discrepancies, understand risk, or judge whether an observation is trustworthy.

APPROVE only when intent, proof and runtime materially agree, required behavior is reachable through the assembled system, and no material unintended behavior was found in reviewed scope. RETURN with the concrete behavioral discrepancy and evidence when behavior is missing, wrong, unreachable, materially contradicted, or proof does not match intent. ESCALATE when intent is ambiguous/contradictory or the observed need requires changing agreed product behavior.
When remediating a deficient review, re-run final review outside-in: Intent, Exercise, Observe, Reconcile, Decide.
avoid: Starting final review while required CI, tests, type, security or active strict convention checks fail; return the failing gate to the responsible implementation phase before spending semantic-review reasoning.
Deriving expected behavior from the delivery diff, implementation or a test body: they show what was built, not what was supposed to be built.

Treating passing tests, a clean diff, green CI or green convention checks as the final behavioral judgment; they are supporting evidence only. Treating a passing end-to-end test as proof without checking what it proves.
Moving inward to an internal function because it is easier to invoke; accepting internal calls, implementation objects, mocks or descriptive tokens instead of the declared observable result.
Reviewing only the lines changed in the delivery.

Reopening naming, decomposition, abstraction, complexity, formatting or other design/style/refactoring questions that passed their governing phase, without concrete evidence of a behavioral defect or delivery risk.
Silently redefining or changing the plan to make the implementation appear correct; using final review to expand scope or redesign.
Approving from static inspection alone when the claim requires runtime observation.
Accepting or approving a delivery despite a material mismatch: a material mismatch blocks delivery.
unless: A delivery intentionally changing no externally observable behavior still requires reconciliation; the reviewer may set the intended invariant to 'no behavioral change' and verify it with the relevant assembled proofs instead of inventing a new user journey.

If the behavior cannot be exercised safely against production dependencies, use the highest faithful environment and boundary the plan authorizes; static-only approval is still not allowed when the claim needs runtime observation.
Ambiguous or contradictory intent is not a reviewer failure and must not be resolved by inference; return ESCALATE so the responsible planning authority settles it.
core.why: Tests and implementation can drift from the plan together while still agreeing with each other; only an intent-first, independent comparison of intent, proof and assembled runtime catches missing, unreachable or semantically drifted behavior that green gates cannot see.
evidence: A durable review record covering: intent sources considered, boundary exercised, observations obtained (the externally meaningful result), discrepancies found, and the final decision (APPROVE, RETURN or ESCALATE).

Supporting runtime evidence: a browser result, a response, a persisted effect, an emitted event, a trace, a routing result plus its business outcome, or equivalent proof. CI status, tests, a clean diff, convention checks, screenshots, traces and runtime output support the judgment but do not replace observing that delivered behavior matches the plan.
The record shows expected behavior was stated from intent artifacts before the diff or implementation was used as reference.
A RETURN names the concrete behavioral discrepancy with evidence. An ESCALATE names the ambiguous, contradictory or change-requiring intent.
verification: No mechanical detector exists for this rule; compliance is judged by an LLM or human reviewer from the durable review record.
Reconciliation succeeds only when declared intent, executable proof and observed runtime describe the same material behavior, and no required outcome is missing or materially contradicted.

What the judgment does not accept: passing tests alone are insufficient (a test may have drifted with the implementation); runtime behavior alone is insufficient if it no longer satisfies declared intent; a correct plan with an unexercised or unreachable implementation is also incomplete.

Decision mapping. APPROVE: intent, proof and observed behavior materially agree. RETURN: required behavior is missing, wrong, unreachable or unexpectedly changed, or is proved by tests that no longer correspond to the plan. ESCALATE: authoritative intent is ambiguous or contradictory, or must itself change before correctness can be judged.

Assembled boundary means the highest meaningful real product-facing boundary, e.g. a user-facing journey, an exposed interface of the assembled system, or a production routing and sequencing path. An internal function chosen because it is easier to invoke does not qualify.

Fix-hint checklist structure: Intent (read criteria; state expected behavior before using diff as oracle), Exercise (gates green; highest boundary; real production path; minimum inputs), Observe (record externally meaningful result plus runtime evidence), Reconcile (intent vs tests, both vs observed; missing/unexpected behavior, unreachable paths, plan/test/implementation drift), Decide (APPROVE/RETURN/ESCALATE).
Severity 4: a material mismatch blocks delivery.

fires: A delivery whose CI and strict convention gates are all green is handed to the final reviewer for acceptance.
A refactor-only delivery that claims no externally observable behavior change reaches final review with green gates.
A delivery with green gates that changes routed behavior (a plan-declared routing decision selecting among behavior paths) is about to be accepted.
doesNotFire: A required CI, test, type, security or strict convention check is still failing. The delivery goes back to its implementation phase instead.
Work is in an implementation phase of the ATDD loop (RED, GREEN or REFACTOR) and the delivery is not yet offered for acceptance.
Static code-quality or style review that runs during an implementation phase.

profileRequirements.meaning: The intent-bearing sections of the stack's plan artifacts that the final reviewer reads as declared intent before relying on diff or implementation, and whose content supplies the routing decisions, behavior sequences and journey that the review looks for.
profileRequirements.bunValue: acceptance criteria, product capability responsibilities, user/system flow sequence, flow router route decisions, exposed journey and delivery criteria

profileRequirements.meaning: The acceptance-level kinds of executable proof whose actually proven behavior is reconciled against declared intent.
The assembled-boundary kinds of executable proof (journeys, routed paths, behavior sequences) whose actually proven behavior is reconciled against declared intent.
profileRequirements.bunValue: route, user/system flow and journey tests

neutralityNotes: This rule is a semantic review policy, so almost all of it is already stack-neutral; the only stack-specific content is the ATDD-Bun plan-intent section list (product capability responsibilities, user/system flow sequence, flow router route decisions, exposed journey, delivery criteria) and the proof-kind list (acceptance, smoke, route, user/system flow and journey tests). The intent sections were generalized to plan-artifact responsibilities/sequences/routing decisions/journeys with the concrete sections supplied by the proposed key idiom.plan_syntax#plan_intent_sections; roles.plan_artifact.kinds is deliberately NOT used for them, because the vocabulary defines it as concrete plan-artifact kinds (e.g. desired_outcome_yaml) — a different concept that bun.json does not instantiate for this rule. The proof kinds are supplied by roles.acceptance_test.kinds and roles.e2e_test.kinds. Nothing was dropped or added: 'strict ATDD Bun gates' (activation fires, verifier fix-hint) was generalized to 'strict convention gates'; 'exposed HTTP/runtime boundary' to 'exposed interface of the assembled system'; 'PR' to 'delivery'. The ATDD loop terms RED/GREEN/REFACTOR were kept: they are methodology phases, not stack machinery. Per rule 7, severity 4 and the mismatch-blocks-delivery disposition stayed in core verification, and the sidecar's '(implementation type: none)' annotation is marked bunOnly.
